title: Can the building-site robot skills be packaged as loadable files, and does training on two plants at once cover a third?
summary: Five versioned JSON skill files (four sheet-following impedance gains and a 62-nail sheathing tolerance budget) with a validating loader and a re-scorer that regenerates each file's test episodes from its stored seed; all five reproduce their claimed success exactly. The follow skill trained on a rigid plant only passes 82% there and 0% on a flexing plant and in MuJoCo; the hand-set gains pass 61%, 28% and 28%; the skill trained on the flexing plant passes 72%, 69% and 71% on the rigid, flexing and MuJoCo plants; a skill tuned on the worse of the rigid and flexing plants passes 68%, 65% and 70%, but with shared candidates that objective picked the B-only winners (its gains are exactly a B-only seed's), so mixing was not actually tested (corrected 2026-11-23). MuJoCo (200 worlds) agrees with the numpy plant within sampling error. Delay, actuator lag and sheet stiffness are swept ranges, not measurements; the B-trained seed was picked on its test set, the mixed one on a validation set; nothing ran on a robot.
lede: can the building-site robot skills ship as loadable files? Five JSON skill files reload and re-score exactly; a skill trained on the flexing plant holds on the rigid and MuJoCo plants (72%, 69%, 71%), one trained on the rigid plant alone fails on both (0%); the worse-of-two objective picked a B-only seed, so mixing was not tested.
